title: Unified runtime profiling exporter: per-kernel attribution + scheduler annotations
creator: Diego Sanchez
description:
Goal: Provide a low-overhead, unified exporter and trace annotations that attribute latency and token costs to specific GPU kernels and runtime scheduler decisions (kernel choice, attention path, prefill vs decode scheduling). This is intended to make root-cause analysis and cost-optimizations (e.g., swapping to a faster attention kernel or enabling chunked attention) observable at request and model-variant granularity.

Scope:
- Define a compact span/NVTX annotation schema that captures: kernel id/name, kernel params (seq_len, kv_cache_state, qkv layout), chosen attention optimization (e.g., flash, chunked, split-QK), and scheduler decision tags (immediate, queued, batched, burst).
- Implement per-kernel micro-timing collection (host-side timestamps + GPU kernel durations) with sampling to keep overhead <1%.
- Map kernel timings back to the originating request/route and model variant in trace spans so Console trace views and per-route dashboards can surface kernel-level hot spots.
- Export aggregated heatmap metrics to Prometheus/Datadog: kernel_name{model,route,attention_mode,seq_bucket} -> p50/p90/p99, calls_total, queued_time_ms.
- Backwards compatible NVTX ranges: preserve existing NVTX ranges but enrich them with compact tags for new tooling; add mapping for older traces in ingestion.

Non-goals: per-thread stack traces, exhaustive GPU counters (we may add later if requested).

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits new, size-limited trace spans for prefill and decode kernel executions with kernel_name and attention_mode tags.
- Exported Prometheus metrics with label cardinality limited by seq_bucket (e.g., 0-32,33-128,129-512) and attention_mode.
- End-to-end PoC dashboards in Console demonstrating identification of a bottleneck kernel and actionable recommendation (e.g., switch to chunked attention for long prefixes).
- Measured overhead on synthetic workload <= 1.0% p50 latency increase and <= 2% p99 on 90% of tested cases.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Use short integer kernel IDs in traces rather than long strings to reduce trace payload; translate IDs at ingestion/Console.
- Sampling strategy: deterministic head-sample (first N requests per-minute per-route) + reservoir-based sampling for long tails. This balances discoverability vs volume.
- We avoid heavy GPU-side instrumentation to keep portability; rely on host timers surrounding kernel launches and occasional GPU timestamps to calibrate drift.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Attribution+Exporter+Spec (draft)
- PoC notebook and perf harness: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1PoC-profiling-exporter
